response.draft:
Slide 1: Ridgeline Return Works
Paid work first. Then a job that lasts.
Reentry employment in Carver Falls, Tamsen County
A request to the Pellwood Foundation: $90,000 toward our FY2027 expansion
Workforce Reentry Round, December 2026

Slide 2: Two Years of Growth
People enrolled: 88 in FY2025, 121 in FY2026 (+38%)
Placed in permanent jobs: 47 in FY2025, 69 in FY2026 (+47%)
Finished the crew phase: 61 in FY2025, 90 in FY2026
Average starting wage: $17.10 in FY2025, $18.25 in FY2026
Employers hiring our people: 15 in FY2025, 23 in FY2026

Slide 3: How It Works
Paid crew work starts within 5 business days of intake
$16.50 an hour on landscaping, light demolition and park cleanup
A job coach helps with ID, resume, driver's license and interviews
Goal: a permanent job within 12 weeks
Then 6 months of support on the job

Slide 4: Six-Month Job Retention
71% of FY2026 placements were still employed at six months (58% in FY2025)
What the number covers: 52 of 69 placements have reached six months
37 of those 52 confirmed employed
The 6 people we lost contact with are counted as not employed
The other 17, placed in spring, are not counted yet
We can't say how much of the gain comes from our program
County unemployment also fell, from 5.1% to 4.4%, and we have no comparison group

Slide 5: In His Words
"The crew paid me the first week. That's the part nobody else did. I didn't have to choose between rent and showing up."
Darnell, finished the crew phase in October, now on the night shift at Brannock Precast

Slide 6: What We Learned in FY2026
Most job losses happen in the first 60 days: transportation, supervision appointments, a first conflict with a boss
People who stayed employed were far more likely to have had 3 or more coach check-ins in those 60 days
Our coaches were spread thin, and follow-up was what slipped
With one crew of 12, some people waited up to 3 weeks to start
4 employers asked for more referrals than we could send

Slide 7: The FY2027 Expansion: $186,000
Second crew lead and crew supervisor stipend: $72,000
Retention coach, full-time with benefits: $64,000
Second crew vehicle lease and equipment: $28,000
Added participant supports: $22,000
FY2027 targets: 160 enrolled, 90 placed, 75% six-month retention
Retention measured the same way, with lost contacts counted as not employed

Slide 8: A Careful Use of Money
FY2026 expenses: $612,400
65% went to program staff and 16% to participant supports
Cost per person enrolled: about $5,060
Cost per permanent placement: about $8,875
Crew wages are paid through the work contracts and are not included in these costs

Slide 9: Our Request
$90,000 from the Pellwood Foundation
That covers about half of the $186,000 expansion
The other $96,000 is being raised from our current funders
The $612,400 base budget is covered by existing sources
Full FY2027 budget: $798,400
Marisol Okafor-Reyes, Executive Director, Ridgeline Return Works, Lowell Street, Carver Falls
